CSS Flexbox

This synthetic technical fixture exercises extraction and preservation of definitions, restrictions and examples in their original order.

Axes and wrapping

Flexbox lays out items in one dimension at a time. The cross axis is perpendicular to the main axis.

Each wrapped line distributes space independently of the other lines.

<div class="box">One</div>

.box {
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
}

CSS Grid

This synthetic technical fixture exercises extraction and preservation of definitions, restrictions and examples in their original order.

Flexible tracks

Grid controls rows and columns together. Unlike independent flex lines, items align in both dimensions.

.wrapper {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr));
}

The minimum track width is 200px, and remaining space is shared.

private restricts storage to private caches. max-age starts when the response was generated, not when received.

HTTP caching

This synthetic technical fixture exercises extraction and preservation of definitions, restrictions and examples in their original order.

Conditional requests

If-Modified-Since and If-None-Match validate cached responses. If-None-Match takes precedence when both are present.

GET /index.html HTTP/1.1
If-Modified-Since: Tue, 22 Feb 2022 22:00:00 GMT
If-None-Match: "33a64df5"

HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
Cache-Control: max-age=3600

Force reload

A normal reload validates; force reload bypasses the cached response.

fetch("/", { cache: "reload" });

TaskGroup gather

This synthetic technical fixture exercises extraction and preservation of definitions, restrictions and examples in their original order.

Task groups

class asyncio.TaskGroup

All tasks are awaited when the context manager exits. The first non-cancellation failure cancels remaining tasks.

async def main():
    async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:
        task1 = tg.create_task(some_coro())
    print(task1.result())
asyncio.gather(*aws, return_exceptions=False)

The first exception is propagated by default. Other awaitables are not cancelled and continue to run.

Lock

This synthetic technical fixture exercises extraction and preservation of definitions, restrictions and examples in their original order.

Synchronization primitives

These primitives are not thread-safe. Methods do not accept timeout; use asyncio.wait_for for timeouts.

class asyncio.Lock

Implements a mutex lock. Acquiring a lock is fair: the first coroutine that started waiting on the lock proceeds first.

lock = asyncio.Lock()
await lock.acquire()
try:
    await use_resource()
finally:
    lock.release()

Releasing an unlocked lock raises RuntimeError.
